abstract: Background Angiographic staging describes large-artery stenosis and collateral evolution in moyamoya disease but does not directly depict the cortical surface vasculature, which can vary among patients with similar Suzuki stages. We examined whether a side-matched three-dimensional retinal vascular measure was associated with intraoperative cortical vascular phenotypes after accounting for Suzuki stage. Methods This prospective single-center cohort included 52 patients with moyamoya disease who underwent combined direct and indirect revascularization; 48 had analyzable retinal vessel volume density (RVVD) in the side-matched eye. RVVD was defined as the percentage of the corresponding retinal tissue volume occupied by three-dimensional optical coherence tomography angiography vascular signal within the central 6 x 6-mm region from the retinal nerve fiber layer to the inner plexiform layer. After dural opening and before vascular manipulation, overall cortical vascular richness and arterial, venous, and small-vessel richness were graded from 0 to 3. Associations were evaluated with Spearman correlation and proportional-odds ordinal logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, and ipsilateral Suzuki stage. Results Mean RVVD was 12.92% (SD, 3.30 percentage points). Higher RVVD was associated with greater overall cortical vascular richness ({rho} =0.523; bias-corrected and accelerated bootstrap 95% CI, 0.279-0.714; P<0.001) and arterial richness ({rho} =0.522; 95% CI, 0.261-0.714; P<0.001). Per 1-SD higher RVVD, the adjusted cumulative odds ratio for being in a higher richness category was 3.92 (95% CI, 1.82-8.44; P<0.001) for overall cortical vascular richness and 4.31 (95% CI, 1.92-9.70; P<0.001) for arterial richness. Conclusions In moyamoya disease, higher side-matched RVVD was associated with richer overall and arterial cortical vascular phenotypes at revascularization surgery, independent of Suzuki stage. Three-dimensional retinal vascular imaging may therefore provide a noninvasive, side-specific preoperative measure of cortical vascular remodeling.
